record.paper_title: Group actions on 4-manifolds: some recent results and open questions
record.context_brief: Homologically trivial prime-order smooth actions on homotopy K3 surfaces
record.original_question: For any prime number p > 2, are there nontrivial smooth Z_p-actions on a homotopy K3 surface that act trivially on homology?

evidence.quote: Question 4.5. For any prime number p > 2, are there any nontrivial but homologically trivial, smooth Zp-actions on a homotopy K3 surface?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A homotopy K3 surface is a closed, smooth, simply connected 4-manifold that is homotopy equivalent to a smooth K3 surface (equivalently, a closed simply connected smooth spin 4-manifold with Euler characteristic 24 and signature -16). A smooth action of a finite group G on such a manifold X is said to be homologically trivial if the induced action on H_*(X; Z) is the identity, and nontrivial if the action of G on X is not the identity action.

Question: Does there exist an odd prime p and a homotopy K3 surface X admitting a nontrivial smooth action of the cyclic group Z/pZ that is homologically trivial? Equivalently, for every odd prime p, determine whether some homotopy K3 surface supports a nontrivial smooth Z/pZ-action acting as the identity on integral homology.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that the analogous question for involutions (p=2) has been studied, with results showing strong restrictions, but no published resolution of the odd-prime case for homotopy K3 surfaces was located. The problem appears to remain open, consistent with its formulation as an open question in the surveyed literature on smooth finite group actions on 4-manifolds.

status_evidence.title: Homologically Trivial Smooth Involutions on K3 Surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Treats the involution (p=2) case, showing strong constraints on smooth homologically trivial involutions on K3.
status_evidence.claim: Only the involution case is settled in the located literature; the odd-prime question is not addressed there.

status_evidence.title: Constructing homologically trivial actions on products of spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs homologically trivial finite group actions on products of spheres, but not on homotopy K3 surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: No construction or obstruction specific to homotopy K3 surfaces and odd primes was found.
